title: Keeping characters consistent in an AI-assisted RPG opening
author: teamJayK
selftext:
I drew the cast and storyboarded the opening for my tactical RPG, Year without a Summer. I made the animation with Claude and Seedance. Seedance generated the shots, and I spent days retouching frames by hand to keep the characters recognizable. For the latest cut, I rebuilt some shots from scratch.



[Full opening on YouTube](https://youtu.be/P29_--a2luk)

comments.author: ProbablyDoesntLikeU
comments.body: Here we go, this is how it's done. Ai as a tool, not just one prompt and calling it done. Thank you for not posting slop. Very cool animation

replies.author: teamJayK
replies.body: Thanks, I really appreciate it! Getting the characters to look like themselves from shot to shot took a lot of trial and error. Glad you liked the opening!

replies.author: teamJayK
replies.body:
I used AI to generate the animation. I designed the giant creature and the characters myself, and I storyboarded and directed the sequence.



Please remove the GIF from your comment and refrain from using my footage, designs, or sequence as a reference or template for your own work. Thank you for understanding.

comments.author: Responsible-Dot-3801
comments.body: I have to say man, this looks peak. It just need a good story. You have something special here.

replies.author: teamJayK
replies.body: Thanks, that means a lot! The story is a big part of why I wanted to make this game in the first place. It’s a historical fantasy set in 1815 Indonesia around the Tambora eruption, and I’m looking forward to sharing more of it.
